claim_summary: Let \(M=\operatorname{GP}(8,3)\) be the Möbius–Kantor graph, and let \(X=\operatorname{Ind}_2(M)\) consist of vertex subsets inducing connected components of size at most two. Then \(X\simeq\bigvee^3 S^6\) integrally. Its full automorphism group \(G=\operatorname{Aut}(M)\), of order \(96\), acts on \(\widetilde H_6(X;\mathbb Q)\) through an absolutely irreducible three-dimensional rational character \(\chi\). For rotation \(r:u_i\mapsto u_{i+1},v_i\mapsto v_{i+1}\), the trace vector \((\chi(r^j))_{j=0}^7\) is \((3,-1,-1,-1,3,-1,-1,-1)\), and the full-group character has average zero and squared norm one. Consequently \(\widetilde H_k(|X|/G;\mathbb Q)=0\) for every \(k\ge0\). The homology-action kernel has order two. This does not assert the quotient is contractible or that an integral equivariant sphere-wedge splitting exists.
integrity_notes: Exact finite enumeration and signed integral chain calculations are supplied in a standalone executable verifier.
Prior ordinary-independence results are distinguished from the two-independence claim.
Originality comparisons are based on identified accessible sources and do not assert a mathematical proof of novelty.
limitations: Restricted to the 16-vertex Möbius–Kantor graph and its two-independence complex.
The sphere-wedge homotopy equivalence is nonequivariant; the full-group representation is rational.
The full symmetry quotient is rationally acyclic, not shown contractible.
No claim of absolute bibliographic completeness or external independent validation.
title: Three six-spheres and an irreducible symmetry character in the Möbius–Kantor two-independence complex
